subject: maths
question: P and Q working alone can complete a work in 5 days and 15 days respectively. They work on alternate days one at a time. P works on the first day. In how many days the whole work will be completed?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 5, 15) = 15 units.

Efficiency: **P** = 3 units/day, **Q** = 1 unit/day.

In a 2-day cycle (**P** + **Q**), work done = 3 + 1 = 4 units.

In 3 cycles (6 days), work done = 4 × 3 = 12 units.

Remaining 3 units (15 − 12) are completed by **P** on the **7th day** (3 ÷ 3 = 1 day).

**∴ The correct answer is 7 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **P** = 5 days

Time taken by **Q** = 15 days

**Formula:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

⇒ Total work done in the first 2 days (P on day 1, Q on day 2) = 3 + 1 = 4 units

⇒ Work done in 6 days (3 cycles) = 4 × 3 = 12 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done after 6 days = 15 − 12 = 3 units

⇒ On the 7th day, it is **P**'s turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by **P** to finish remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of P = 3 ÷ 3 = 1 day

⇒ Total days required = 6 + 1 = 7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In alternate work problems, calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days if there are 2 people) and then determine how many full cycles fit into the total work.

Total Work and Efficiency

Total Work = Time × Efficiency. Efficiency is the rate of work done per unit of time and is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Remaining Work Calculation

Time for remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of the person whose turn it is next. Always check who starts the work on the first day.</p
